$comment: Per-file allowances for scripts/ci/check_fabricated_facts.py. A count may fall and may never rise; a file absent here may have none. Every rule records the owner accountable for retiring its remainder and the date by which that must happen - an expired allowance fails the check, which is what stops a ratchet becoming permanent.

fabricated_observation_literal.reason: Three colonies survive the Work/Environment eradication. state/constants.rs declares LEGACY_UNRECORDED_AT, the sentinel ~20 Session-event projections substitute when an event carries no epoch; retiring it means making those wire times Option, which is a Managed-projection change rather than a store fix. control/models.rs stamps a catalog entry with a frozen created_at because a model has no registration event here and the upstream wire forbids null; it needs a Control-owned publication instant. official_request_witnesses.rs builds a synthetic pagination cursor whose created_at is a cursor position, not a record's observation.

ambient_clock_read.reason: The wall clock predates the WallClock port across the worker, runtime and control tiers. Each file is converted by taking a WallClock at construction or the caller's sampled instant as an argument; the count may only fall. The scan was widened to Utc::now, concrete clock values read in place (SystemClock.now_ms(), Clock::now_ms(&SystemClock)), cfg(any(test, feature)) code that ships with its feature, and files that declare their own clock trait (no longer exempt); that raised the recorded 167 reads in 97 files to 190 in 110 without any new read being written. The model-request budget and retry work then added three (provider-genai, the runtime inference engine), and the BOOTTIME authority clock moved local-process's read into awaken-authority-clock: 193 in 110. Run ingress, the container sandbox's waits and warm pool, the Worker's registration and evidence loops and the Session application now read monotonic time through awaken_lease_contract::mono (Stopwatch, MonoDeadline) and wall time through their injected clock; what remains in the Worker lifecycle is paired with the BOOTTIME authority proof's scheduling Instant, and the container effect-fence and egress reads wait on the runtime-host composition that builds those providers. The Managed adapter's rate limit, Skill, Memory-store, Deployment and Work routes and its projection timings read the Resources, Deployment, Session or Coordinator clock they are composed with, and the Deployment application stamps on its injected clock. Every remaining monotonic reading outside the Worker lifecycle's authority proof and the model-inference clock (the OAuth token cache, MCP progress throttling, the circuit breaker, tool timing, image-build and shutdown waits, the FUSE drain and content cache, Dream and evaluation timings) now goes through awaken_lease_contract::mono. The Coordinator's application access (issuance, revocation, expiry, retention), fleet readiness, claim-fenced Artifact publication, claimed commits, operator quarantine and Dream processes stamp and judge on the Coordinator clock they are composed with. The Runtime's and the native provider's inference timing read mono instead of the retired TokioModelInferenceClock.

clock_trait_declaration.reason: Each context declared its own wall-clock port before awaken-lease-contract owned one: agent-contract Clock, WorkerClock, RegistryClock, DataSubjectClock, WarmLeaseClock and the runtime ModelInferenceClock. Each is retired by taking awaken_lease_contract::WallClock; the count may only fall. The last, ModelInferenceClock, is gone: inference policy reads awaken_lease_contract::mono and ModelAttemptTiming carries MonoDeadlines. No clock trait remains outside awaken-lease-contract.

defaulted_system_clock.reason: Constructors that pick the real clock themselves (Arc::new(System*Clock), system_clock() below the root). Each is retired by making the clock a required constructor argument that the composition root supplies once; the count may only fall. The Worker transport now requires its clock: that removed eight defaults (worker-transport-security, run-ingress-http, awaken-cli lib.rs) and moved three to the test-support Scenario compositions that have no process clock yet (coordinator lib.rs scenario mounts, scenario-host main); the process compositions that choose the one clock are registered roots. The Resources clock slice removed the registry's own default and the ambient File, Memory-store and Repository stamps, and the Scenario compositions (coordinator test-support mounts, scenario-host deployment) now choose the Resources clock themselves (three more), until they receive a process clock. The commit stores now require their clock (the in-memory and filesystem coordinators silently read the host clock before); the dev harnesses that build them (awaken-eval runners, the coding-agent example library, the Scenario host) choose it where they compose, which adds four such calls while removing the Coordinator runtime authority's own default. The Host now carries the process clock its composition chooses: the dispatch pool, reconciler, recovery drive, child scheduler and ephemeral authority read it instead of each choosing the real clock (five removed); the one left is the test-support fixture constructor, whose fixture is its own composition. The Worker builder and its embedder entry points require the clock, and the example and Scenario Worker mains choose it. The Session application and its binding sink require the clock too (two removed): product startup passes the process clock and the Scenario Session state passes the Host's, while the volatile ManagedState fixture constructor chooses it where it composes (one added). Nineteen more are gone: the dispatch test harness, the Vault surface, the in-memory Environment and Work stores and the store conformance suites take the clock; the Scenario mounts read the Host's; the Managed fixture constructor takes it from its testkit; and the Scenario host, evaluation runners and coding example are registered harness roots. The runtime-host restructuring retired the Host fixture constructor's and the container environment builder's choice; the one left is live control, whose clock argument its runtime-host callers must supply.

shadow_clock_helper.reason: Private fn now*() helpers that read time without a port, plus the now methods of the per-context clock traits. Each is retired by reading the injected WallClock (WallClockExt::now_ms/observed_at) or by retiring its trait; the count may only fall. The Session application exposes its clock instead of a now_unix_ms helper. The Managed routes' now_ms helpers are gone; the Vault's fail-closed clock reading is a named reading of its injected clock. The Coordinator's access-store, Dream, quarantine and Dream-application helpers are gone. The ModelInferenceClock trait's now() and its Tokio adapter are gone.
